governing: block shear of the bracket plate (AISC 360-22 J4.3), block of 2 rows and 1 column at the plate corner
notes: final.petra is try4.petra unchanged; petra check gave PASS, 15 of 15 obligations certified. Bracket: 5/16 in A572 Gr 50 plate bolted to the W12x40 flange (A992) with 8 bolts, 7/8 in A325-N (bolt_group.120, threads included), snug-tight, standard holes, 4 rows x 2 columns, pitch 2-3/4 in, gauge 5 in, Lev 1-7/8 in, Leh 1-3/8 in. Plate depth is 12 in. ASD, service shear 0 to 39.889 kip at e = 8 in. Highest utilisations: block shear 0.954; bolts 0.951 (most loaded bolt 15.44 kip by the elastic method against 16.24 kip A325-N single shear); flexural rupture 0.864; shear rupture 0.818; plate lateral-torsional buckling 0.814. Detailing: pitch 0.848 of the 2-2/3 d minimum; flange edge distance (8.01 - 5)/2 = 1.5 in; room to tighten clear of the web. Petra checks bolt tearout only toward the top and bottom edges. I also checked tearout by hand along each bolt's elastic-method force direction in the plate and the flange. The worst case is the inner-column end bolt pushing toward the plate's side edge: 10.6 kip against 11.2 kip (0.945). That case is why Leh is 1-3/8 in; at 1-1/4 in it fails. The bracket plate must reach from 1-3/8 in inside the inner bolt line to at least the load line, 8 in from the bolt-group centroid (5.5 in past the outer bolt line). Not checked: how the load is delivered to the plate at the load line, and the column member itself. A 5-1/2 in gauge also passes (try3, governing 0.940) at slightly more plate weight.
